title: Declarative Permission Inference and Middleware Shim for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a declarative permission inference engine plus a lightweight middleware shim that unifies authorization checks for API, serving runtime, and Console routes under RBAC v2. Unlike previous work that focused on a monolithic policy evaluator, this ticket implements a compiler that transforms declarative permission manifests into optimized runtime checks and attaches a small, low-latency middleware to enforce decisions and emit structured audit events.
design_notes:
Goals: 1) Reduce authorization latency by moving common predicates to compile-time and using an in-memory index for attribute lookups. 2) Provide a single enforcement contract that works for HTTP API, internal gRPC serving/runtime, and Console UI routes. 3) Emit a stable audit envelope that downstream sinks (Kafka, BigQuery) can consume without additional enrichment.

Core components:
- Permission manifest schema (YAML/JSON) with resources, actions, and derived roles.
- Compiler that generates two artifacts: an optimized decision trie and a compact feature descriptor for each route.
- Middleware shim that loads the trie, evaluates decisions with short-circuit paths, and attaches audit metadata to request contexts.
- Fallback path: when a required attribute is unavailable, middleware defers to the central policy service with an async enrichment option.

Trade-offs: favor low p99 latency over complete expressivity. Complex temporal or graph-based policies will be flagged for central evaluation rather than compiled inline.
api_spec:
Enforcement API (middleware-facing):
- Check(resource:string, action:string, subject: {id:string, attrs: map<string,string>}) -> {allow: boolean, reason: string, matched_clause: string | null}
- Explain(token:string) -> string (human-readable explanation used in admin UI)
- EnrichAttributes(subject_id, keys[]) -> async job id (when local attrs missing)

Console integration: middleware attaches 'x-rw-auth' header for downstream services with JSON-serialized allow/assertion and an audit id. For internal gRPC, use trailer metadata 'rw-auth-audit-id'.
middleware_flow:
1) On request entry, middleware extracts subject (JWT / session cookie) and requested resource/action derived from route metadata.
2) Look up subject attributes in local attribute cache; if stale or missing, consult attribute fetcher with a 50ms budget.
3) Run compiled trie evaluator; if match -> return allow with short-circuit.
4) If no compiled match and policy complexity marker present -> call Control Plane Policy API (synchronous, 200ms SLA), attach reason and fallback policy id.
5) Emit audit event (synchronous light envelope + async full payload) and continue request lifecycle.

Notes: We will ship shims for Express, FastAPI, and the internal Go HTTP framework. gRPC interceptors for runtime paths will mirror the same decision call semantics.
audit_schema:
AuditEnvelope v1:
- audit_id: uuid
- timestamp: RFC3339
- principal: {id, type, source} (string fields)
- resource: {type, id}
- action: string
- decision: allow|deny|deferred
- reason: string (short)
- matched_compiled_clause: optional string
- evaluation_path: compressed token (base64)
- attributes_snapshot: optional map serialized as JSON string
- trace_context: string

Delivery: synchronous small envelope to kafka.audit.events, full event materialized to s3 for compliance retention. All fields are strings to avoid schema drift in downstream consumers.
sso_saml_plan:
SSO integration checklist:
- Ensure middleware supports subject source == 'saml' and maps SAML attributes to local attribute keys.
- Create attribute mapping table for common IdP attributes (email, groups, department, entitlements).
- For SAML-initiated flows, the middleware should accept a short-lived session token and rehydrate attributes from session storage; avoid calling IdP per request.
- Add unit tests for group membership expansion and for edge cases where the IdP sends unexpected attribute names.
- Coordinate with IAM team to add new SAML mappings: Confluence ticket CON-98765.

SSO session TTL recommendation: 15 minutes for high-privilege routes, 60 minutes for read-only console pages.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gate 'rbac_v2_compiled_checks' off by default.
2) Stage 1 (canary): enable for internal platform service only (~5% traffic) with detailed debug logs and sampling of full policy API calls.
3) Stage 2 (team opt-in): enable for Console read routes for specific orgs with no admin role.
4) Stage 3 (wider): enable for runtime read-only and embedding endpoints.
5) Stage 4 (safest): enable for write/admin routes only after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.

Monitoring and rollback: track auth latency p50/p95/p99, false-deny rate (compared to central policy baseline), and audit event failure rate. Automatic kill switch if false-deny > 0.2% in production or p99 latency regresses by >30%.
testing_plan:
- Unit: compiler correctness tests for manifest -> trie translation; expect equivalence with reference evaluator.
- Integration: middleware + test policy manifests running in a staging cluster; fuzz attributes to ensure no silent allowed-by-default paths.
- Load: simulate 10k rps with mixed cache-hit rates (90% hit / 10% miss) and assert p99 auth latency < 12ms on optimized path.
- Security: threat modeling session for attribute spoofing and replay attacks; add tests for header tampering and JWT key rotation.
- Compliance: run audit export and retention verification against S3 lifecycle policies.

Automated test jobs: rbac-compiler-ci, auth-middleware-integration, rbac-load-smoke.
open_questions: Should complex graph-based entitlements (e.g., resource-owner-of-ancestor) be supported by compiled trie or redirected to central PDP?
What is the authoritative source for attribute freshness on high-privilege checks (cache TTL vs synchronous fetch)?
Do we want the middleware to return a distinguishable HTTP header when a decision is 'deferred' to central policy?

acceptance_criteria:
1) Compiler converts manifest examples in /specs into a trie artifact and unit tests verify semantic equivalence with the central evaluator.
2) Middleware implements Check(...) API and returns allow/deny with <12ms p99 on compiled path under load target (10k rps).
3) AuditEnvelope v1 is emitted on every auth decision and ingested by kafka.audit.events with schema validation passing.
4) SSO/SAML attributes map is validated with at least two IdPs in staging and session TTLs honored.
5) Feature flag + rollout plan executed with monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback configured.
